objectives: Use diagnostic evidence to select a specific bl-cycle skill for practice.
Re-teach the diagnosed component with explicit modelling and guided examples.
Demonstrate transfer on 15 fresh reassessment items.
Advance at or above 80%; continue targeted support below the threshold.
concepts: Remediation should match the component shown by diagnostic evidence.
Sound-recognition errors need listening contrasts; decoding errors need blending practice.
Encoding errors need segmentation and grapheme mapping; comprehension errors need text evidence.
Fresh reassessment checks transfer after teaching.

definitions.definition: Focused teaching and practice for a diagnosed learning need.
A new assessment after targeted instruction.
A fresh example that checks whether a skill generalises.
The minimum score required to advance.

workedExamples.solution: Model /b/ /l/ smoothly, use sound boxes, then decode fresh bl-words.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner writes black as bak.
workedExamples.solution: Segment the word, map both initial consonants and the taught ck ending, then read it back.
Reread the sentence, locate the place phrase and point to the text evidence.

commonMistakes: Repeating every lesson instead of targeting the diagnosed component.
Reusing the diagnostic questions during reassessment.
Using speed alone as evidence of fluency.
keyTakeaways: Select the practice path from component-level evidence.
Model, practise with feedback, then use fresh items.

revisionPoints: Decoding: blend every phoneme in order.
Encoding: segment and map all graphemes.
Comprehension: reread and point to text evidence.
studyMaterial.weakTopicRevision: If reassessment remains below 80%, continue focused practice on the same diagnosed component, then use a new set of items before routing again.

conceptual.prompt: Why must reassessment items be fresh?
conceptual.answer: To test transfer instead of memorised answers.
The component shown as weak by diagnostic evidence.

application.answer: Blend /b/ and /l/ without an extra vowel to read blush.

application.prompt: Which practice helps a learner who omits l when reading?
application.answer: Guided blending with sound boxes and fresh bl-words.

application.prompt: What route applies to 11 out of 15?

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How can you distinguish a decoding need from a comprehension need?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Check whether the word was decoded accurately and whether the learner can use text evidence.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why not repeat the same diagnostic after practice?
higherOrderThinking.answer: The learner may remember answers without transferring the skill.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What should happen after a score of 13 out of 15?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Advance because 13/15 is above the 80% threshold.

mixedReview.answer: Read the word back and check each grapheme.

mixedReview.prompt: What evidence supports a literal answer?
mixedReview.answer: The exact words in the sentence or passage

questions.question: What are the first two phonemes in blush?
Which word begins with bl and rhymes with mess?
What is the onset in bless?
Which word has a different rime from bless?
Read: “A black block is on the mat.” What is on the mat?
Read: “Ben can dab a blob.” What action does Ben do?
A learner says “buh-lush.” What feedback is best?
options: Blend /b/ and /l/ without an extra vowel

questions.question: Which word contains bl and the rime -ink?
What best supports a literal comprehension answer?
options: Pointing to the exact sentence words
Using a detail not in the text

questions.question: Which is the best fluency goal after practice?
options: Read accurately and smoothly while keeping meaning
Read as fast as possible even if words are skipped

questions.question: If a learner scores 11 out of 15 on fresh reassessment, what happens next?
options: Continue targeted remediation because 11 is below 12/15
Repeat the same questions until memorised

answerKeys.explanation: Bless shares the -ess rime with mess.
Blush keeps bl at the start and sh at the end.
The onset is bl; the rime is -ess.
Block ends in -ock, while the others share -ess.
The sentence directly says a black block is on the mat.
Dab is the action stated in the sentence.
The blend should remain smooth without an inserted vowel.
Literal answers should be supported by explicit text evidence.
Fluency includes accuracy, smoothness and comprehension.
Eleven is below the 80% threshold of 12 correct out of 15.
